name: Tychicus
source_summary: A beloved brother and faithful minister described by Paul as entrusted to carry his letters to the Ephesian and Colossian churches and to report on Paul's circumstances and encourage their hearts, later sent to Ephesus and considered for a mission to Crete.
family_friendly_summary: Tychicus was one of Paul's most trusted companions and messengers. Paul entrusted him with carrying his letters to the churches in Ephesus and Colossae, and specifically asked him to tell those believers how Paul was doing and to encourage their hearts in person, since a letter alone couldn't convey everything. Paul calls him 'a beloved brother and faithful servant in the Lord,' high praise reflecting years of dependable partnership. Tychicus was also sent by Paul to Ephesus at another point, and Paul considered sending him to Crete as well. Tychicus's story shows the vital, often overlooked role of a trusted messenger who faithfully carries both words and encouragement between a minister and the churches he serves.
adult_story: Tychicus, from the province of Asia, is named among Paul's traveling companions carrying the collection to Jerusalem (Acts 20:4), but his more significant role emerges as Paul's trusted courier and personal representative to churches he could not visit himself. Writing from prison, Paul describes him as the one who will bring news of his own situation to the Ephesian believers: 'Tychicus, the beloved brother and faithful servant in the Lord, will make everything known to you... that you may know about us, and that he may comfort your hearts' (Ephesians 6:21-22). Paul entrusted him with the same dual role for the Colossian church, again calling him 'the beloved brother and faithful servant and fellow bond-servant in the Lord,' explicitly sent 'for this very purpose, that you may know about our circumstances and that he may encourage your hearts' (Colossians 4:7-8) -- Tychicus's mission was not simply to deliver a letter but to provide personal reassurance and pastoral encouragement no letter alone could fully carry. Near the end of Paul's ministry, Paul mentions sending Tychicus to Ephesus, likely to relieve Timothy so Timothy could come to Paul (2 Timothy 4:12), and Paul also considered sending either Artemas or Tychicus to relieve Titus on Crete so Titus, too, could come to him (Titus 3:12). Across every mention, Tychicus appears consistently as a dependable, trusted, and pastorally sensitive messenger central to how Paul kept his scattered churches connected and encouraged.
devotionals: Tychicus’s story teaches us about trusted messenger; may we look to Jesus, whose grace and truth never fail.
Through Tychicus’s experience of faithful service, God teaches us to trust His wisdom and follow Jesus faithfully.
